description: Use it when the user wants captions or subtitles burned into a video, to read with the sound off, karaoke style or in the brand's fonts, clear of an app's buttons. Burns captions into a video from words with times the user already has: a speech-to-text JSON with word or line times, from OpenAI, whisper.cpp, Deepgram and others, an SRT or WebVTT file, or a demo's steps file, whose step notes become the captions. It does not listen, and no tool here makes such a file. karaoke shows each caption whole and lights the word being spoken, line shows whole captions, word one word at a time. The captions sit inside the space every place in for leaves free of its buttons, drawn by Chrome on this machine in the fonts and color given and laid over the video in one ffmpeg encode, its sound copied. Writes captioned.mp4, captions.srt, captions.vtt, captions.ass, words.json, sheet.png (captions on their frames, the picture to look at first), safe-zones.png (a frame under each app's buttons) and CAPTIONS.md, which the result shows. For the subtitle files alone, use make_subtitles instead. The captions playbook (makersmcp_playbook) has the whole job. (easycaptionkit 0.1.5, on this machine.)

box.description: A dark box behind the words instead of an outline.

brand.description: A brand kit, its folder or brand.json: its button, link or logo color lights the spoken word, and without fonts or font its heading font is asked for by name, which this machine may not have. make_brand_kit makes one.

font.description: A font family to draw with, from fonts.css or this machine, like Inter.

fonts.description: A font kit, its folder or fonts.css: the captions are drawn with the site's own font files, its heading font first. make_font_kit makes one.

for.description: The places the video goes to: the captions keep clear of the buttons of every one of them at once (default: the places of the video's shape).

highlight.description: The spoken word's color, like #ffd23f, in the karaoke and word styles; a dark one lights the word on a patch of it.

libass.description: Draw the captions with ffmpeg's libass instead of Chrome, for a machine where Chrome cannot start; it needs an ffmpeg built with libass, and for a font kit's WOFF2 files one whose FreeType reads WOFF2, and draws no color emoji.

lines.description: Lines a caption may take, 1 to 3 (default 2); the word style shows one.

max_chars.description: Characters a line may take, 8 to 80 (default: what fits the safe width, at most 42).

out_dir.description: Folder to save into, absolute or relative to /tmp/churn-hnvpfmca. Default: <video-folder>/easycaptionkit-<video-name>, where <video-name> is the name of video without its extension and <video-folder> is the folder video is in. A run replaces the files an earlier run of this kit left there, so give each version its own out_dir.

position.description: Where in the free space the captions sit (default bottom): middle or top when the picture has text or a face at the bottom of it.

size.description: The letters' size in percent of a phone's width, or of the frame's short side, 2 to 20 (default 6.5, or 9.5 for the word style). A line too wide for the free space is drawn smaller.

style.description: karaoke lights the word being spoken in each whole caption (default karaoke), line shows whole captions in one color, word one word at a time, bigger.

video.description: The video to caption, any file ffmpeg reads. A launch film's film.timeline.json beside it is copied as captioned.timeline.json, so check_video finds its cuts.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the result, counted from the start of the call, before returning a job_id to wait on. Some clients end a call after 60 or 240 seconds; 45 is safe in all of them.

words.description: The words and their times: a speech-to-text JSON, an SRT or WebVTT file, a demo's steps.json, or the words.json of an earlier run with a misheard word fixed by hand. Not an ASS file.

name: caption_video

continued.description: True when this call continued the job an identical call started, instead of starting another.

docs.description: The notes the text shows, and where each one is.

expires_at.description: When the download links stop working.

url.description: Where to download the file, when the job ran on a server.

folder.description: Where the kit saved its files.

last_line.description: What the kit was doing last.

next.description: What to do next, as the Next line says.

passed.description: For checks: whether the check passed.

title: Captions burned into a video
